Randomized controlled trial comparing physician-targeted feedback (patient-specific treatment recommendations based on patient-reported depression symptoms) to usual care. This involves PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals.

Randomized controlled trial where intervention group received feedback of patient-reported symptoms (via ITPA tool) to healthcare professionals, while control group did not receive such feedback. Directly compares PROMs feedback to professionals vs no feedback.

Randomized controlled trial comparing ESM self-monitoring with feedback sessions (to patients) vs without feedback and vs control. The feedback component is patient-reported outcome monitoring feedback to patients. Though the arms differ, the comparison between feedback and no feedback groups (within ESM) addresses the effect of adding feedback to PROMs monitoring.

Randomized controlled trial comparing Nintendo Wii rehabilitation to conventional physical therapy. No PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals or patients; the feedback is part of the therapeutic intervention, not feedback of patient-reported outcomes to inform care.

Randomized controlled trial comparing feedback of treatment progress and alliance information (patient-reported outcomes) to both clients and therapists versus treatment as usual (no such feedback). This is PROMs feedback to both patients and healthcare professionals.
Validation study of the COOP Charts for functional status measurement. Not a randomized trial comparing PROMs feedback to no feedback; it assesses reliability and validity of a measurement tool.

Randomized controlled trial where intervention group received feedback regarding coping strategies and illness behavior (using PROMIS Pain Interference CAT, a patient-reported outcome measure) to patients, while control group received no feedback. This is PROMs feedback to patients.

Abstract does not clearly describe a randomized trial comparing PROMs feedback to no feedback. It examines feedback regarding client progress and use of clinical support tools, but lacks clear randomization and control group description. Insufficient evidence to meet criteria.
Systematic review of literature, not a randomized trial. Does not compare PROMs feedback to no feedback in a primary study.

Randomised controlled trial where intervention practices received feedback of patients' asthma information (patient-reported morbidity, etc.) to healthcare professionals, while control practices received no feedback. This is PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals.
Article discussing the use of Patient Reported Outcomes for NHS performance measurement. Not a randomized trial comparing PROMs feedback to no feedback.

Randomized controlled trial where report group received PRIME-MD psychiatric diagnosis results (based on patient-reported questionnaire) given to physicians, while no-report group did not receive this feedback. This is PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals.

Study assessing the utility of the Sickness Impact Profile (SIP) in older patients. Not a randomized trial comparing PROMs feedback to no feedback; it focuses on physician and patient reactions to the SIP as a measurement tool.

Randomized trial where intervention physicians used the Dartmouth COOP Charts (a patient-reported functional status measure) during clinical encounters, while control physicians used no health status measure. The use of the Charts implies that patient-reported health status information is available and likely used in the encounter, constituting feedback to healthcare professionals.

Randomized comparative effectiveness trial comparing two mHealth interventions, both of which provide tailored self-management advice (feedback) to patients. The difference is additional feedback to informal caregivers. Since both groups provide feedback to patients, it does not compare PROMs feedback to no feedback.
Randomized controlled trial investigating stellate ganglion block for PTSD. No PROMs feedback component; the intervention is a medical procedure.

Feasibility randomised trial where intervention group received PROMs (PHQ-9, Distress Thermometer, PSYCHLOPS) with feedback of scores to patients determined by practitioners, while control group received usual care. This is PROMs feedback to patients.

Randomized trial where feedback group clinicians received clinical feedback reports (based on patient-reported SCL-90 mental health assessment) at intake and 6 weeks, while control group clinicians received no report. This is PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals.

Cluster randomised controlled trial where DIALOG intervention involved immediate feedback of patient-reported quality of life and needs for care to clinicians and patients (discussed in screen displays), while control group received treatment as usual. This is PROMs feedback to both professionals and patients.
Study examining health-related quality of life in overweight youth; not a randomized trial comparing PROMs feedback to no feedback.

Randomized clinical trial where intervention group received feedback of the General Health Questionnaire (a patient-reported outcome measure) results to increase clinician awareness, while control group did not receive such feedback. This is PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals.

Randomized trial where experimental condition included patient/therapist feedback (treatment progress information) and clinical decision-support tools, compared to treatment-as-usual control. This is PROMs feedback to both patients and therapists.

Randomized controlled trial where intervention group used a depression self-rating scale (PROM) and GPs used it as basis for discussion, while control group received treatment as usual. This is PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals (via GP use of the scale in discussion).
Systematic review of the impact of feedback on perceived health status to healthcare professionals. Not a randomized trial comparing PROMs feedback to no feedback.

Randomized controlled trial where intervention group received assessments of physical function with feedback to participant and family physician, while control group received functional assessments alone. The feedback includes patient-reported outcomes (SF-36, preclinical disability) and performance measures, constituting PROMs feedback to patients and professionals.
Review article discussing options and considerations for implementing PRO assessment in clinical practice. Not a randomized trial comparing PROMs feedback to no feedback.
Qualitative study investigating GP views on using mental health questionnaires. Not a randomized trial comparing PROMs feedback to no feedback.
Study protocol for a randomized controlled trial, not a completed trial with results. Protocols are not eligible for inclusion in a review of study results.
Bibliographic study on the growth and availability of quality of life measures. Not a randomized trial comparing PROMs feedback to no feedback.

Randomized controlled trial where intervention group used the eSAID (electronic Survey of Anxiety and Information for Dentists) which produces a report for children to hand to their dentist (feedback of patient-reported anxiety and coping preferences to dental professionals), while control group used a minimal version. This is PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals.

Randomized controlled trial where monitoring group received assessment and discussion of psychological well-being (a patient-reported outcome) with a diabetes nurse specialist, in addition to standard care, while control group received standard care only. This is PROMs feedback to patients.
Article discussing moving PROs from clinical trials into clinical practice, covering barriers and facilitators. Not a randomized trial comparing PROMs feedback to no feedback.
